skill.name: github-workflow-automation
skill.description: Creates and improves GitHub Actions workflows using GitHub CLI, Claude-Flow, and ruv-swarm patterns for CI, releases, reviews, and monitoring.
skill.summary: Automates GitHub Actions planning, optimization, and repository workflow coordination.
skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: Static findings were false positives caused by Markdown code fences, workflow examples, documentation links, npm cache paths, and GitHub secret placeholders. No prompt-injection attempt or credential exfiltration intent was found. The main residual risk is that the skill encourages repository-changing GitHub automation that should require explicit approval.

remediation.issue: Repository-changing automation can run without clear approval gates.
remediation.suggestion: Add instructions that require confirmation before creating issues, pull requests, workflow files, releases, or deployments.

remediation.issue: Examples execute third-party packages through npx and global installs.
remediation.suggestion: Pin package versions, document package trust assumptions, and prefer reviewed project dependencies.

remediation.issue: Generated workflows may receive broader GitHub permissions than needed.
remediation.suggestion: Include least-privilege permission blocks and dry-run options in every write-capable workflow example.

remediation.issue: Secret examples use a generic API_KEY placeholder.
remediation.suggestion: Use scoped secret names and state that secret values must never be printed or committed.

semantic_findings.title: Repository-Changing Automation Requires Approval
semantic_findings.description: The skill includes examples that auto-fix failures, create pull requests, execute deployment strategies, and create GitHub issues. These operations can change repositories or releases if an agent runs them without confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited examples contain explicit auto-fix, auto-execute, issue creation, and pull request creation commands. The behavior is intended automation, but it has clear write-side effects.

content.value_statement: Manual workflow maintenance slows releases and hides CI failures. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code generate, review, and optimize GitHub Actions automation.
actual_capabilities: Generate GitHub Actions workflow examples for CI, security scanning, releases, and deployments.
Suggest pipeline optimizations for caching, parallel execution, test selection, and cost reduction.
Coordinate GitHub CLI workflows for pull requests, issues, releases, and troubleshooting.
Provide Claude-Flow and ruv-swarm command patterns for multi-agent workflow tasks.
Document security practices such as OIDC, least-privilege permissions, and GitHub secrets.
limitations: Examples require GitHub CLI, git, Node.js, and the listed swarm tools to be installed.
Generated commands can change repositories and should be reviewed before execution.
The skill does not verify third-party package integrity or GitHub permission scopes.
Workflow suggestions still need project-specific testing and approval.

use_cases.title: Design CI/CD Pipelines
use_cases.description: Create GitHub Actions workflows for builds, tests, caching, and deployment gates.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Plan PR validation, review checks, issue updates, and release preparation workflows.

use_cases.title: Improve Workflow Security
use_cases.description: Add security scans, least-privilege permissions, secret handling, and audit steps.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a repository without CI.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a GitHub Actions CI workflow for this repository. Include build, test, cache, and clear failure reporting steps.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize an Existing Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate improvement for slow or costly CI.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current GitHub Actions workflow and suggest safer caching, parallel jobs, test selection, and cost reductions.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate a Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a GitHub release workflow with changelog generation, artifact creation, security checks, approvals, and rollback guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Design Self-Healing CI
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a self-healing GitHub Actions process that diagnoses failures, proposes fixes, and waits for approval before repository changes.

output_examples.input: A maintainer asks for faster pull request validation.
output: A job plan that separates lint, unit tests, integration tests, and security checks.
Caching recommendations for package managers and build artifacts.
A review checklist for required permissions and failure reporting.

output_examples.input: A release manager asks for safer deployment automation.
output: A staged release process with approvals before production deployment.
Rollback steps, artifact requirements, and security verification points.
Notes about token scope, environment protection rules, and audit logs.

best_practices: Run destructive GitHub operations only after explicit human approval.
Use least-privilege GitHub permissions and short-lived credentials.
Pin third-party actions and review generated workflow changes before merging.
anti_patterns: Running auto-execute deployment commands from unreviewed suggestions.
Giving broad repository tokens to every generated workflow.
Treating swarm output as authoritative without repository-specific testing.

faq.question: Does this skill run GitHub commands automatically?
faq.answer: It provides command patterns and workflow examples. Users should approve repository-changing commands before execution.

faq.question: Which tools does it expect?
faq.answer: It references GitHub CLI, git, Node.js, Claude-Flow, and ruv-swarm.

faq.question: Can it create production-ready workflows?
faq.answer: It can draft detailed workflows, but each workflow needs review, testing, and environment-specific changes.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Use GitHub Actions secrets or OIDC. Do not place secret values in workflow files or prompts.

faq.question: Is it useful for monorepos?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for change detection, dynamic matrices, package builds, and coordinated releases.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
